summary: The missions and work list refreshers no longer give up during a burst of changes. A fold still changing after its chunked catch-up rounds keeps its rows, and the next fold continues from them. Every snapshot still refolds at most 100 rows.

replay.detail: No replay trigger or recovery wait. The lists are in-memory publications folded from the existing projections.

schema.detail: No tables, columns, indexes or migrations.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rule, registry or coordinated member upgrade change.

compatibility.detail: Published rows are the ones the direct read gives at the publication's cut, as before. Nothing is written, replicated or sent differently, so mixed-version fleets interoperate unchanged. A fold runs at most three catch-up rounds, and no snapshot refolds more than 100 rows.

downtime.detail: No storage migration or added startup work.

manual.detail: Nothing to configure. During a burst the previous publication stays served until a fold reaches one cut. The refresher no longer logs 'kept changing in ways no short fold can follow' or withdraws the list for a burst. It does so only when a catch-up round must fold from nothing: more than 10,000 claims since the rows' cut or, for the work list, a replica repair. Rebuild counts gain 'pending: missions kept changing' and 'pending: work kept changing'.

recovery.detail: An older build goes back to giving up after three chunked rounds. Nothing is stored, and pending rows live only in memory.
